segments.narration: Candles were lit at noon across New England. On May 19, 1780, daylight vanished completely without warning.
Roosters roosted, cattle retreated to barns, and terrified crowds filled churches, believing Judgment Day had arrived.
Black soot rained from the sky, yet no local fires were burning. What could blot out the sun across five colonies?
Tree ring analysis in Canada finally revealed the cause: massive forest fires in Ontario sent an enormous soot cloud into the upper atmosphere.
Driven by high winds, that giant soot blanket blocked the sun, turning wildfire smoke into an apocalyptic legend.
